samples.summary: The canonical `/api/v1` reference doc is not updated for any of the five new route groups this change adds. `docs/design/rest-api.md` enumerates the whole surface endpoint-by-endpoint (§5.2 Tabs lists only GET/POST/PATCH, §5.4 lists the tab-scoped POST verbs, §5.5 says the content routes serve `doc`/`slides`/`note`), and the diff adds: `DELETE /tabs/:tid`, `POST /tabs/:tid/reorder`, `POST /tabs/:tid/duplicate`, `GET|PUT /tabs/:tid/images`, `GET /layouts` + `POST|DELETE /slides/...`, `board` on the content routes, and the entire `/comments` tree — none of which appear anywhere in the doc (grep for `comments`/`board` in rest-api.md returns nothing). The `reorder`-instead-of-`move` naming exception, the docs-thread creation refusal, and the destructive replace rule for worksheet images exist only as code comments. CONTRIBUTING requires the design doc to move with the architecture; only `notifications.md` and `sheets/comments.md` were touched. Nested `docs/design/sheets/sheet-image.md` likewise has no record of the new endpoint pair.

`docs/design/cli.md` §4 command tree and §8.4 safety-annotation table are the documented contract for the CLI surface, and neither records the new commands the diff registers (`comments *`, `board content|set-content`, `sheets images get|set`, `slides layouts`, `slides slide add|duplicate|move|delete`, `sheets tabs delete|move|duplicate`). The tree at :430 still shows `tabs` with `list` only, and the safety table (:1595-1631) stops at `sheets.charts.set`, so the new `destructive` entries (`comments.delete`, `sheets.images.set`, `board.set-content`) are unlisted. `packages/cli/README.md`'s command tree (:85-113) is stale in the same way. The registry in `packages/cli/src/schema/registry.ts` was updated, so behaviour is fine — this is documentation drift only.

The capability-audit doc this change repeatedly cites as its motivation ('the capability audit in docs/design/agentic-office-workflow.md filed them under class B') is not updated. Classes A and A′ each carry a '> **Status note** (Step N of the todo, landed after this audit)' paragraph recording the close while leaving the measured table intact (:141-151, :167-172). Class B (:207-217 — Comments 6, Slide granular editing 5, Tab rearrange 3, Sheet floating images 2, Board 2) is exactly what this diff closes, and gets no such note, so the doc still asserts 'No command can close these' and 'docs-content.controller.ts:94 rejects any type that is not doc / slides / note' — now false.

The mention grammar moved from `packages/frontend/src/components/comments/mentions.ts` to `@wafflebase/sheets`' `comment/mentions.ts`, but its own design doc still presents the frontend file as the implementation home ('### New shared helper — `packages/frontend/src/components/comments/mentions.ts`', and §21-24 'The work lands entirely in the shared frontend comments module'). Only `notifications.md` records the move, in passing. The repo files docs by subsystem, so the canonical mentions doc — not a neighbouring one — should carry where the grammar now lives and why (two readers: editor and backend). Behaviour is unaffected because the frontend module re-exports.

samples.summary: `PATCH .../comments/:threadId/comments/:commentId` (edit a comment, author-only) is implemented in the backend controller and covered by its spec, but there is no `editComment` method on `HttpClient`, no `comments edit` CLI leaf, and no `comments.edit` schema-registry entry — grepping packages/cli/src for `editComment`/`comments edit` returns nothing. Since the whole point of closing class B is reachability from the agent surface, an edit verb that only raw HTTP can reach is a half-exposed capability (and one that no parity test will catch: nothing enforces registry↔endpoint coverage). Either wire it through or drop the endpoint.

samples.summary: Third independent declaration of the board data model. `@wafflebase/board` already owns it (`packages/board/src/model/board.ts:22` — `BoardModel { meta: { title; unit?: 'in'|'cm'; recentColors? }; elements: Element[] }`), and the frontend has `YorkieBoardRoot` + `initialBoardRoot()` with the same `'Untitled board'` default (`packages/frontend/src/types/board-document.ts:3-9`). The new backend `BoardMeta`/`BoardDocument`/`initialBoardRoot()` restates all of it, including the default title string, rather than depending on `@wafflebase/board` (backend package.json depends on sheets/docs/slides but not board). A future board meta field will now have to be added in three places, and the API validator's notion of a board can silently drift from the package that defines one. The docblock acknowledges the mirroring but only names the frontend copy, not the shared package.

CRDT thread-detach logic is duplicated rather than shared. `copyThread`/`copyComment`/anchor detachment/Long⇄number coercion already exist in the frontend stores (`packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/yorkie-comment-store.ts:100`, `packages/frontend/src/app/files/comments/pdf-comment-store.ts:77`, whose `copyAnchor` this file's docblock cites), and `comment-ops.ts` re-states them for the backend. This change already established the right pattern for exactly this problem — it moved `mentions`/`notify-plan` into `@wafflebase/sheets` because two copies of the notification rule had diverged on the preview text — but stopped short of doing the same for the serialization layer, which is the part that decides what an API read of a thread looks like versus what the editor sees. Divergence here means the two surfaces disagree about a thread's shape.

Unrelated change bundled into the feature diff: the workspace-slug uniqueness fix (`Date.now()` → seq + uuid suffix) is a test-infra flakiness fix with no connection to the class-B capability work. Harmless, but it belongs in its own commit/PR so the feature diff stays about the feature.

finding.summary: The new prototype-key guard is applied in one controller only; ~10 sibling v1 controllers do the identical `root.sheets?.[tabId]` lookup-then-write and are left unguarded
finding.evidence: The delta adds `UNSAFE_TAB_IDS` / `assertPlainTabId` as a private helper inside `worksheet-images.controller.ts` and calls it from `worksheetOrThrow` and `getImages`. Its own docblock argues the hazard is generic: "`:tabId` reaches this controller straight off the URL … On a plain object … `sheets['__proto__']` answers `Object.prototype`: truthy, so the NotFound guard passes". That reasoning applies verbatim to every other v1 worksheet controller, none of which was changed: `worksheet.controller.ts:46-50` (`worksheetOrThrow`, then `ws.frozenRows = …`), `worksheet-rules.controller.ts:59`, `worksheet-styles.controller.ts:54`, `worksheet-charts.controller.ts:49`, `worksheet-dimensions.controller.ts:57` (and its six `doc.getRoot().sheets?.[tabId]` writers), `worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:47`, `cells.controller.ts:88/125/158/193/230`, `comments.controller.ts:237/323/559/730`, and `tabs.controller.ts:251` (`if (!root.tabs?.[tabId]) …` immediately before `duplicateTab` writes `root.sheets[newTabId]`). Fixing one of eleven identical call sites places the check at the wrong layer (per-controller private function rather than the shared worksheet-lookup helper the rest of the surface uses) and leaves the stated defect reachable through the other ten routes.

verdict.reason: The finding claims the prototype-key guard exists only as a private helper (`assertPlainTabId`/`UNSAFE_TAB_IDS`) inside worksheet-images.controller.ts, leaving ~10 sibling controllers doing unguarded `root.sheets?.[tabId]` lookup-then-write. Both halves are false in this tree. (1) The guard is a shared module: packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-lookup.util.ts exports `findWorksheet`/`worksheetOrThrow`, whose docblock (lines 4-35) contains verbatim the hazard reasoning quoted in the finding, and whose check is a key-membership test through `safeWorksheetRecordKeys` (line 41) covering both the plain-object `__proto__` case and the Yorkie proxy trap names (`toJSON`/`getID`/...). No `assertPlainTabId` or `UNSAFE_TAB_IDS` identifier exists anywhere in the repository. (2) Every controller named as unguarded imports and uses that shared helper at precisely the cited lines: worksheet.controller.ts:14 imports it and lines 73/120/167 call `worksheetOrThrow(root, tabId)` before `ws.frozenRows = ...`; worksheet-images.controller.ts:19 imports the shared util rather than defining a private one; likewise worksheet-rules (21/83/126), worksheet-styles (17/79/120), worksheet-charts (12/88), worksheet-dimensions (16/118/161/204/247, all six writers), worksheet-filter-pivot (11/72/119), cells (29/89/125/158/192/228), comments (58/329/333), worksheet-structure (31/169/231/283). tabs.controller.ts:259 uses the same membership test via `safeWorksheetRecordKeys(root.tabs).includes(tabId)` before duplication, not the truthiness check described. A dedicated spec (worksheet-lookup.util.spec.ts:70-114) exercises `__proto__` on plain roots and proxy-trap names. The only remaining raw `root.sheets?.[tabId]` reads (comments.controller.ts:238, 562/567, 733) take tabId from internal state (`root.tabOrder`, `tabIdOfThread`), not from the URL, and lines 234-236 document that choice. The check therefore already sits at the shared worksheet-lookup layer the finding asks for, and covers all the cited routes.
